checks.note: LoginRateLimiter.claim loops on tryAcquireIdentifierLock with Thread.sleep(50ms) up to CLAIM_WAIT (2s) inside a Propagation.MANDATORY transaction (checkLimited), so the caller's pooled connection stays bound to the thread for the whole wait; nothing releases or suspends it, so a same-key burst exceeding pool size parks every connection. (Caveat load test not runnable here — only this file provided — but the hold is structurally certain.)

CoachRegistrationService.registerCoach does call user.setLogin(req.email()) with no case normalization in this file, but the claimed consequence depends on CoachRegistrationRequest.email() (possible normalization in the record), User.setLogin, AuthService.login's lower-casing, and the user.login column type — none shown here.

registerAccount does set login to the raw-case email and toUser (user.setLogin) copies it unchanged while lower-casing only email, but the user is persisted via UserRegistrationService.createUser, which may normalize the login, and the lower-cased findOneByLogin lookup in AuthService.login is not shown. Whether authentication actually fails depends on those two classes.

registerPlayer wraps only `userRepository.save(user)` (not saveAndFlush) in its try/catch, and the in-file AC10 comment in verifyEmail confirms this codebase's @Tsid ids defer the INSERT to flush — so the unique-constraint violation surfaces at commit, outside the catch. The catch also maps only to security.emailInUse; there is no phoneInUse mapping anywhere in registerPlayer.

Confirmed: the grace-window branch in AuthService.refresh resolves a replayed token via findFirstByUserIdAndUsedFalseAndExpiresAtAfterOrderByCreatedAtDesc(ownerId), the user's newest live token with no successor linkage, then rotates and marks it used — hijacking another device's token when that token is newer than the replayed token's successor, whose later refresh hits markAllUsedByUserId/invalidateSessionsForUser; the branch also issues a replayer a fresh session. Caveat: the finding's own repro ordering fails (A's successor A2 is newer than B1, so B is unaffected); the trigger requires B to log in after A's first refresh.

R9 is at verifyPhone and smells the OTP guess-budget weakness (fresh bucket per resend, inconsistent limits) but misses the core mechanism: in-memory per-JVM state and no DB-side invalidation of the OTP.
R8 describes the same bcrypt-skip timing oracle in AuthService.login enabling email enumeration.
R6 targets sendPasswordResetMail and notes divergent responses reveal account existence, but via the dob-NPE paths rather than the success-vs-PWD_RESET_REJECTED distinction.
No reported finding addresses per-target throttling of resendVerificationEmail.
No reported finding mentions activate.security or the permit-all authorization path in SecurityConfiguration.
